newsitem.title: USA: U.S corp bond new issue mart bustles with activity.
newsitem.headline: U.S corp bond new issue mart bustles with activity.

text.p: The corporate bond primary market continues to bustle with activity as issuers get set to bring new supply to market and hungry investors line up for more, dealers said.
"We should should see a lot of business today," said one syndicate source. "Abbey National, Campbell Soup, and a few preferreds are expected...and then whatever surprises that may be in the wings."
Abbey National Plc is expected to tap the market with $300 million in a noncall 10-year perpetual bond via Salomon Brothers, sources said.
In addition, Campbell Soup Co will launch a corporate debt offering on Wednesday, lead underwriter Goldman Sachs & Co said.
"The Campbell Soup deal will be launched today," a high-grade syndicate source at Goldman said.
The underwriter had no further commment on the details of the offering; however, market sources said the deal is expected to consist of $300 million in 10-year debt.
Price talk on the issue is 35 to 38 basis points over U.S. Treasuries, sources added.
Goodyear is set to issue $100 million in 10-year debt via Goldman Sachs & Co, dealers said.
Also, British Sky Broadcasting is expected to issue $300 million in Baa3/BBB-minus rated 10-year yankee debt via Goldman Sachs & Co, syndicate sources said.
Dealers expect supply will continue to flow in at a steady pace as an improved interest rate environment and investor demand for paper create a favorable environment for issuance.
"We're in a positive issuing enviornment...the market is holding steady," another syndicate source said. "Deals were met with very good by investors.

Among private placement issues, Rayovac is expected to price $100 million in 144A senior subordinated notes due 2006 via Donaldson Lufkin and Jenrette Securities. Price talk on the issue is 10.25 to 10.50 percent, sources said.
Meanwhile, dealers said preferred deals have been on the rise and leading to a large buildup in the new issue calendar.
"There's a huge calendar for preferred deals," said one syndicate source. "In the same way yankee issuance dominated a few weeks ago, preferreds are now dominating the calendar."
Turning to Tuesday's business, Citicorp priced $200 million in A2/A rated subordinated notes to yield 77 basis points over U.S. Treasuries via Bear Stearns & Co.
In the government market, the 30-year U.S. Treasury bond is off 16/32 at 98-10/32 to yield 6.88 percent.
